title: Dedicated capacity intake & prioritization playbook for enterprise requests
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Synthesis and triage playbook to intake enterprise requests for Dedicated capacity. Goal: create a repeatable rubric and decision flow for translating customer asks into standardized scope (SLA targets, reserved throughput commitments, GPU class requests, and scaling policies). This ticket consolidates stakeholder feedback from Solutions Eng, Sales, and Customer Success and proposes a scoring model, templated intake form, and an escalation path for exceptional cases. The playbook is intended to reduce subjective prioritization, speed quote turnaround, and produce consistent contract SLAs and engineering handoffs.
acceptance_criteria: A templated intake form (questions + required metrics) exists and is used by Sales/Solutions for new enterprise Dedicated asks
A prioritization rubric with scoring guidance (SLA risk, revenue commitment, regulatory constraints, technical complexity, support burden) is documented and reviewed by Eng and Sales
Default recommended SLAs and reserved throughput bands are proposed with mapping to GPU classes (e.g., small/medium/large workloads -> T4/A100/H100 guidance)
Escalation flow for 'high risk' or non-standard GPU requests documented (who signs off, SLA delta, cost multipliers)
Handoff checklist for Eng (runbook, expected traffic pattern, KV caching needs, fallbacks) and legal (contract language snippets) provided
comments: 2026-02-21 - Aisha K: Initial consolidation of customer asks from Q4 sales deck and Solutions notes. Noting repeated asks for guaranteed p95 latency and reserved tokens/min. Draft intake form attached.

2026-02-25 - Lina Chen (Solutions Eng): Suggested measurement fields: expected concurrency, average prompt length (tokens), peak burst window (minutes), acceptable cold-start latency, preferred region. Also flagged that some customers expect H100-class GPUs for generative video prototypes.

2026-03-01 - Miguel T (PM): Added prioritization weights proposal. Proposed weights: revenue (30%), SLA strictness/regulatory (25%), complexity & implementability (20%), risk to fleet/operational burden (15%), strategic value (10%). Requesting Eng review for feasibility and guardrails.

2026-03-05 - Raj Patel (Eng Lead): Reviewed. Engineering recommends mapping reserved throughput bands to expected GPU footprint ranges and adding a compatibility constraint for model families that require >48GB memory. Also proposed automatic fallback policies as a required ask for any committed SLA.

2026-03-10 - Legal: Provided contract language snippets for per-minute throttling, penalty caps, and out-of-scope denial-of-service protections. Recommended adding an explicit maintenance blackout window clause.

2026-03-12 - Sales: Ran playbook against two active deals. Outcome: cut quote turnaround time from 7 days to 48 hours for standard cases. One non-standard request escalated per the flow and sent to Architecture review.
next_steps: Finalize intake form and embed in Sales playbook, schedule 60-minute alignment with Eng and Solutions to agree scoring thresholds, pilot the playbook on 3 live deals, and create a small automations backlog item to pre-populate responses from usage telemetry.
decision_summary: Adopt a weighted scoring rubric and three reserved throughput bands (S/M/L) mapping to suggested GPU classes. Require an automatic fallback policy for every committed SLA. Non-standard hardware requests require Architecture + Reliability sign-off and a scoped runbook. Legal to insert standardized SLA clauses into contract templates.
